title: The person's permission for a loosening may also be a file the console writes under the person's login, bound to the proposal it showed

looked_in: person_word in harness_ledger_entry.schema.json and harness_proposal.schema.json: one form, words said in a seat's window
check 89's landing rule in contracts/validate.py: a landed loosen, retire or core change needs person_word

the console-signed plan approval as built: plan_approval signed_through {via, login} (e2f5b08b), the person's login in microscope_runtime/envelope/console_login.json (4e61cf96), check 41 holding approvals/ to the person (088fb2b0), plan.md 15.1 item 4
INC-20261018-05: the same schemas could not hold a loosening before the person was asked; same class, a different gap

changes.owner: a manager, with manager-console-office-20261017-1 for the console's shape
changes.change: The file the console's server writes at the moment the person types the password again on the administrator screen, and nothing else writes, at microscope_runtime/approvals/harness/<HP-nnn>-<first 12 of proposal_sha256>.json: {artifact: harness_permission, schema_version, proposal: HP-<nnn>, proposal_commit: <40 hex>, proposal_sha256: <64 hex>, decision: yes|no, screen_words, signed_at, signed_through: {via: console, login}}, no other key. proposal_sha256 is over the bytes of contracts/harness/proposals/<id>.json at proposal_commit, which is what the screen showed. screen_words is the screen's own sentence the person confirmed, naming the proposal id and that hash. The login is a plain id in plan_approval's signed_through pattern. No password, hash of one, or token can ride in it.

person_word keeps its four fields, and a console word fills them so: quote is the file's screen_words verbatim, said_in_window_of is 'console:<login>', on is signed_at's date, recorded_in is the file's path. The schemas admit the 'console:' form of said_in_window_of; nothing else changes in them.

For a person_word whose said_in_window_of starts 'console:', at a landed or refused line: (1) recorded_in is a path under microscope_runtime/approvals/harness/, present in the tree being judged, and every commit that touched it was made under human; (2) the file validates as harness_permission, names this line's proposal, and its decision is yes for landed and no for refused; quote equals screen_words and on equals signed_at's date; (3) the login after 'console:', signed_through.login and the login in microscope_runtime/envelope/console_login.json are equal byte for byte. That file is the one the person places by hand, never the console's settings, so any other login, a test login among them, binds nothing; (4) proposal_sha256 equals the sha256 of the proposal file's blob at proposal_commit, read from git, and the file name carries its first 12; (5) what was signed is what lands: the proposal's kind, changes, touches_core, answers, needs_threshold and revert in the judged tree equal the signed blob's. The hash is of the blob at proposal_commit and not of the file at landing, because proof, reach and notes are filled in after the person signs and may differ; (6) the console form counts for kind loosen and retire with touches_core empty. A proposal that touches the core still needs words said in a window, until the person says otherwise (see notes).

The folder reuses the person's approvals guard: check 41 refuses every seat under approvals/ since 088fb2b0, the runtime's settings deny approvals/**, and the person accepted the console writing into the approvals folder (55a635b6). The operator globs only approvals/*.json, so it never reads these as plan approvals. The change is a fixture: a seat committing a file under microscope_runtime/approvals/harness/ is refused, watched failing, so the subfolder is shown covered and not assumed.

Show the proposal as it stands at a named commit, with its sha256. Ask the password again at each permission. Write the one file at that moment, under microscope_runtime/approvals/harness/, and nothing else. Sign nothing when the folder is absent. A password a session has seen cannot sign, which holds the administrator account until the person changes its password at the console (plan.md 6.1, 1d3f2c97). The screen never lands, reverts, schedules or seats anything. The person commits the file, as an approval.
Rule 1's words gain the console form on 6.1's conditions, citing 659c2214, and name the folder.

revert: git revert <each landing commit>, the check's last
notes: A loosening that touches the core (rule 1), so the person's word is required and given: the line quoted above, said in the intake seat's window and committed verbatim at 659c2214, which counts for every seat from that commit. Scope is read narrowly from the person's words, which name a proposal that loosens a rule. A retirement is a loosening and is included. A change to the core is not named there, so it stays words in a window until the person says otherwise. That is put to the person as a plain question through the intake seat. What the guard rests on, as for the plan approval (plan.md 15.1): check 89 cannot tell a file the console wrote from one any process wrote into that folder. So the folder's guard (check 41 held to the person, the person's own commit, the runtime's denial) and the login file are the whole guard. Folder and person_word shape revised on 2026-10-23 to architecture-20261003-1's proposal, before anything was built. Nothing in it is built until 8.3's words and the check exist. No loosening is landed on a console permission before then.
